sections.h2: Which Rye does this page cover?
sections.html:
This page covers the Town of Rye in Westchester County, which is a different municipality from the City of Rye. The town is made up of the Village of Port Chester, the Village of Rye Brook and the Rye Neck section of the Village of Mamaroneck, and the town itself says it holds around 11,000 parcels. The City of Rye became independent in 1942, so a house inside the city is handled by city offices, and the town assessor has no file on it.

The town comes in two separate pieces: Rye Neck lies to the southwest, apart from Rye Brook and Port Chester. Work out which village your street belongs to first. That one fact tells you who issues permits, who bills the village portion of your tax and which building department holds your certificate of occupancy.

The Census Bureau counts 50,011 people in the town in mid-2025, up 0.8% from 2020. The town's facts and history page places it about 30 miles north of New York City on Long Island Sound, with two Metro-North stations, I-95 and I-287 in or near the south and the county airport and I-684 near the north.

sections.h2: What are the ways to sell fast in the Town of Rye?
sections.html:
Speed here is a function of two things: the shape the house is in and the date you need the money.

  • Broker listing: suits a house that photographs well, if you can live with showings and a buyer's mortgage clock. The town's sales data page can help you gauge price, and a written net-proceeds estimate shows what you keep.
  • Owner-handled sale: no broker fee, but you field every inquiry and negotiate the contract with your own attorney.
  • Investor purchase for cash: the buyer takes the property as is. Estates, tenant-occupied two-families, and houses carrying open violations are the usual candidates.

At Westchester prices, a few percentage points between a listing and a cash offer become real money, so line up the final check from each path. We can send a cash figure for a Port Chester, Rye Brook or Rye Neck house on request.

sections.h2: How do the Town of Rye's housing figures read?
sections.html:
Owners live in 57.9% of the town's homes, and the middle owner-occupied value is $689,400, roughly double the $332,700 shown for the United States on the same Census table.

Median monthly owner costs with a mortgage are reported as $4,000 or more, the top reporting band. With 49.7% of residents age 5 and over speaking a language other than English at home, a listing that offers a bilingual contact can reach more of the buyers who live nearby.

sections.h2: What is the tax and assessment calendar in the Town of Rye?
sections.html:
The assessor says the town values property at 100% of market value, so the number on your assessment should match what the house would bring. The cycle runs on a handful of dates.

  • May 1 is taxable status date, and also the cutoff for exemption filings.
  • The tentative roll is posted June 1, and grievance day falls on the third Tuesday of June.
  • Decisions from the Board of Assessment Review are mailed around September 15, when the final roll is filed.
  • Billing years differ by levy: county and town taxes follow the calendar year, village taxes run June to May, and school taxes run July to June.

The Receiver of Taxes takes payments and mail at 222 Grace Church Street, third floor, Port Chester. The Port Chester and Rye Brook village bills are each paid in two installments with their own windows.

To challenge a value, submit Form RP-524 to the assessment office by hand, through the secure drop box, or as a PDF by email to the address on the town's page. A mailed form has to be in the office by 8 p.m. on grievance day, and a postmark that same day is late. Owners of one-to-three-family homes who disagree with the board can file a small claims petition electronically with the county clerk within 30 days of the final roll, which puts the deadline on October 15.

sections.h2: Which exemptions should a Rye seller or buyer know about?
sections.html:
The assessor needs exemption applications and renewals, senior citizen ones included, by May 1 each year. Basic and Enhanced STAR have moved to the state: new homeowners register with the Department of Taxation and Finance, and the town's assessor no longer takes STAR forms.

That matters at a sale because the town tells new homeowners to register with the state for the STAR credit check themselves. Limited-income seniors, alternative and Cold War veterans, and volunteer firefighters can apply through the assessor. Westchester County raised its veterans exemption caps in 2021, which the town page describes in detail.

Tell your buyer early so they do not assume your current bill carries over untouched.

sections.h2: Where do I find permits and the certificate of occupancy for a Town of Rye house?
sections.html:
The town has no building or planning department of its own. Each village runs those functions, so your village building department holds the permits and the certificate of occupancy.

The assessor's property record card shows the use the assessor knows about, and the town stresses that the card is not proof of legal use. Before listing, look for these:

  • Permits and final sign-offs for any addition, finished basement or garage conversion.
  • The certificate of occupancy, which states the authorized use.
  • Zoning district and map, which come from the village building or planning office.
  • Radius and abutter search instructions, which also come from the village building department.

A cash buyer can often take the house with a paperwork gap still open, though the offer will reflect the cost of curing it.

sections.h2: What does recording a deed in Westchester cost, and what is the transfer tax?
sections.html:
Westchester's County Clerk records the deed through its online PREP portal, which also builds the cover page, the state TP-584 and the RP-5217 report. The clerk's schedule works out to $190 for a three-page residential deed in a single municipality: a $45 statutory fee, $5 a page, $5 for the TP-584 and $125 for the RP-5217.

State transfer tax adds $2 for each $500 of price, rounded up. For the town's middle value of $689,400 that is $2,758. The 1% mansion tax starts at $1 million and falls on the buyer. The clerk accepts transfer tax by ACH, certified or bank check, attorney escrow check or a check from an approved vendor, while credit cards cover fees only.

sections.h2: What draws buyers to Port Chester, Rye Brook and Rye Neck?
sections.html:
Port Chester became a village in 1868 and still runs under that original charter. The town describes it as the Restaurant Capital of Westchester County, and says the restored Capitol Theatre remains a cornerstone of its visitor economy. Rye Brook is the newest village, incorporated in 1982, and Rye Neck is the Mamaroneck-side piece to the southwest.

The town itself keeps two parks: Rye Town Park with Oakland Beach beside Playland, and Crawford Park in Rye Brook with its mansion and sports fields. Commuters weigh the two Metro-North stations and I-95 against the northern highways, while others value being a short distance from Connecticut. Mention whichever of these fits your street in your listing.

faqs.q: Is the Town of Rye the City of Rye?
faqs.a: No. The town contains Port Chester, Rye Brook and Rye Neck, while the City of Rye became independent of the town in 1942. Your tax bill and village will show which one applies.

faqs.q: When is grievance day for Rye property owners in the town?
faqs.a: Third Tuesday of June. The tentative roll appears June 1, which leaves roughly two weeks to file Form RP-524 with the assessor.

faqs.q: Can I sell my Port Chester or Rye Brook house without a certificate of occupancy?
faqs.a: You can try, but the buyer or their attorney will probably raise it. Ask the village building department what it has on record, and mention any gap to a cash buyer at the start.

faqs.q: What would a $700,000 sale owe in New York transfer tax?
faqs.a: $2,800. Divide $700,000 by $500 to get 1,400 units, then multiply by $2. Sellers pay it by default.

faqs.q: Where do Town of Rye tax payments go?
faqs.a: Mail them to the Receiver of Taxes at 222 Grace Church Street, third floor, Port Chester, NY 10573. The town's tax schedule page lists separate due periods for Port Chester, Rye Brook and Mamaroneck village taxes.
